summary: Albert von Le Coq was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied at the Seminar for Oriental Languages (~1900–1902). He held posts at the Ethnologisches Museum Berlin (~1902–1925), becoming Director of the Asian Department in 1914.

Alberto Pelissero is an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the University of Turin (~1979–1984) and Sapienza University of Rome (~1985–1989). He became an Associate Professor at the University of Turin around 2001.

Alberto Todeschini is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He was a guest at Kyoto University and held posts at the University of Trento (attested 2009) and the Italian School of East Asian Studies (attested 2010).

Albertus Bruining was a religious studies and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Amsterdam and at Leiden University (~1864–1871) under Paul Deussen and doctoral supervisor Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern. He became Professor of Theology at Amsterdam in 1900.

Albertus Wilhelmus van den Hoek was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Amsterdam and Leiden University, where he studied under Jan C. Heesterman, as well as under Louis Dumont. He served as head at Leiden University (1989–1992).
Albinas Rimka was a scholar in Indology and other fields. He taught economics at Vytautas Magnus University (1923–1925) and at Vilnius University in 1940.

Albion Moonlight Butters is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar educated at UC Santa Cruz, Harvard, and Columbia under Robert A. F. Thurman and others. He was an Adjunct Lecturer at the University of Turku (2013–2020) and Editor for Khyentse Vision Project (2021).

Albrecht Hanisch is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who completed his doctorate at the University of Marburg under Michael Hahn by 2000. He served with the Nepalese-German Manuscript Cataloguing Project (2007–2014) and the Nepal Research Centre (attested 2013–2018).

Albrecht Weber was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Breslau, Bonn, and Berlin under Stenzler, Lassen, Gildemeister, and Kuhn. He served at Humboldt University of Berlin (1848–1901) and was a member of the Prussian Academy of Sciences.

Albrecht Wezler was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the University of Tübingen under Paul Thieme (~1960–1965). He was Director at the University of Hamburg (1973–2003) and served as Director General of the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (1982–2002).

Aleix Ruiz-Falqués is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics who earned his PhD at the University of Cambridge under Eivind Kahrs. He has held positions at Shan State Buddhist University, the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, and the Pali Text Society.

Aleksander Brückner was a linguist, historian, and archaeologist who studied at the University of Lviv, University of Vienna, and Frederick William University Berlin, studying under August Leskien. He held academic posts at the University of Lviv (~1878–1881) and Berlin (~1881–1924).

Aleksander Dunin Borkowski was an Indology scholar. He pursued philological studies at Chernivtsi University (1827), the University of Lviv (~1827–1831), and the University of Königsberg (~1831–1833), where he studied under Peter von Bohlen.

Aleksandr Arnol'dovich Freiman was an Iranian and Central Asian studies linguist. Educated at Saint Petersburg State University and Giessen under Christian Bartholomae and others, he became Professor of Iranian Philology at Saint Petersburg and worked at the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Aleksandr Gilferding was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Viktor Grigorovich at Moscow State University (1852–1853). He served in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, presided over the Slavic Benevolent Society (1867), and led the Russian Geographical Society (~1869–1872).

Aleksandr Ivanovich Aleksandrov was a linguist educated at Kazan State University under Baudouin de Courtenay and Kruszewski, and at Tartu. He held professorships at the University of Kharkiv, Kazan State University (1888–1911), and Kazan Theological Academy (1912).

Aleksandr Ivanovich Tomson was a linguist who studied at Saint Petersburg State University (1882–1887) under Filipp Fortunatov and Theodor Korsch. He served as ordinary Professor of Indo-European Linguistics and Sanskrit at Odesa University from 1897 to 1932.

Aleksandr Leonovič Grjunberg-Cvetinovič was a linguist, Iranian, Central Asian, and Indology scholar. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Ivan Ivanovich Zarubin, later holding posts there (~1955–1995) and at the Institute of Linguistic Studies (~1960–1995).

Aleksandr Lvovich Duvernois was a linguist who studied at Moscow State University (1855–1866) under Pavel Jakovlevič Petrov. He later served as Professor of Comparative Linguistics at Moscow State University (~1869–1886).

Aleksandr Mervart was an Indologist and linguist who completed his PhD at Heidelberg University (~1904–1907). He served at Kunstkamera as head of the Indian Department (1913) and Keeper (1924–1930), and taught at Saint Petersburg State University (1924–1930).
